kaps_punt: daar is baie verskillende soorte lewende dinge; lewende plante en diere kan al die sewe lewensprosesse uitvoer: voeding, groei, reproduseer, asemhaling, uitskeiding, sintuie, beweging; sommige dinge lyk nie lewendig nie (soos droë bone, droë gis, 'n bevrugte voëleier), maar kan weer 'leef' in die regte omstandighede

items.bewering: Rondom jou leef baie duisende soorte plante en diere.
items.bron: SANBI plant checklist statistics (opus.sanbi.org, 2024) and Le Roux & Klopper 2025 (repository.up.ac.za): about 20 200 indigenous plant species in South Africa alone, before any animal is counted. 'Baie duisende' is a safe reading of 'around you' in the sense of the living world a learner lives in.

items.bewering: Die gras onder jou voete leef, en die kewer op die blaar leef ook.
items.bron: Grass is a plant and a beetle an animal; both carry out the seven life processes listed in the MRS GREN convention (twinkl.com teaching wiki; savemyexams.com IGCSE 'Characteristics of living organisms').

items.bewering: Plante en diere het al sewe die lewensprosesse, nie net een of twee nie.
items.bron: The seven-process convention (movement, respiration, sensitivity, growth, reproduction, excretion, nutrition) applied to plants and animals: twinkl.com 'What are the Seven Life Processes?'; savemyexams.com IGCSE revision note; plants included under movement via growth toward light. It is a teaching convention (some lists add cells or transport) and the lesson's own CAPS bullet states it; true at Grade 4.

items.bewering: Selfs broodmuf en kieme is lewende dinge.
items.bron: Bread mould is a fungus (Rhizopus stolonifer; EBSCO Research Starter 'Black bread mold'; bio.libretexts.org 'Rhizopus'). Germs: KidsHealth (Nemours) 'What Are Germs?' - 'germs are tiny organisms, or living things, that can cause disease'. Caveat a person may want to know: germs include viruses, whose living status is genuinely debated among scientists (Microbiology Society 'Are viruses alive?'; Science News; weet.co.za notes 'geen konsensus'). The lesson's generic statement matches how reputable children's health sources teach it and does not lead a Grade 4 learner to a false conclusion, and the lesson never claims what every germ does (see 'Baie kieme eet').

items.bewering: Die muf groei op ou brood, leef daarvan en versprei oor die brood.
items.bron: EBSCO Research Starter 'Black bread mold' and bio.libretexts.org 'Rhizopus': hyphae draw nutrients from the bread; stolons and spores spread the mould across the surface.

items.bewering: Elke lewende ding het kos nodig om te lewe.
items.bron: Nutrition is one of the universal characteristics of life: organisms obtain and use food for energy and growth; plants make theirs, animals eat others (savemyexams.com IGCSE; vedantu.com 'Life processes'). Universal quantifier holds because 'kos' covers food a plant makes itself, as the next sentence says.

items.bewering: 'n Koei vreet gras, en 'n leeu vreet vleis.
items.bron: Cattle: Noble Research Institute 'Food requirements for different animals' (cattle eat primarily grass); NDSU Farm Research 1989 (grasses dominate grazing cattle diets). Lion: Kuku Group Ranch diet study, Wildlife Research (publish.csiro.au WR22019) - prey animals made up the diet.

items.bewering: 'n Groen plant maak sy eie kos in sy blare met sonlig.
items.bron: nagwa.com photosynthesis explainer and general educational sources: in most plants photosynthesis takes place mainly in the leaves, using light energy (any green part can photosynthesise; the lesson does not say 'only'). Sound simplification at Grade 4.

items.bewering: Lewende dinge word groter en sterker en verander bietjie vir bietjie.
items.bron: Growth as a lasting increase in size, with development, is a characteristic of living things (vedantu.com 'Life processes'; twinkl.com). 'Sterker' is a child-level gloss and not misleading.

items.bewering: 'n Klein saadjie kan oor baie jare 'n boom word.
items.bron: Trees reach maturity over roughly a decade to a century or more depending on species (general horticultural sources found; weak individually but uncontroversial, and 'kan oor baie jare' makes no specific claim).

items.bewering: 'n Kuiken kry vere en word 'n hen of 'n haan.
items.bron: University of Nebraska-Lincoln Extension 'Chick Growth and Development' poster (4H.unl.edu; lancaster.unl.edu): chicks hatch in down, first feathers from a few days, down replaced by feathers between 1 and 5 weeks.

items.bewering: Lewende dinge kan nuwe lewende dinge van hulle eie soort maak.
items.bron: Reproduction as a characteristic of life (savemyexams.com IGCSE; vedantu.com 'Life processes'). 'Kan' avoids implying that every individual reproduces.

items.bewering: 'n Hen lê eiers, en uit 'n bevrugte eier kom 'n klein kuiken.
items.bron: Penn State Extension 'Where chick life begins' (abe.psu.edu): only a fertilised egg carries an embryo that can develop into a chick when incubated; unfertilised eggs do not. Matches the lesson's restriction to 'n bevrugte eier.

items.bewering: Baie plante maak sade, en uit een saad kom 'n nuwe plant.
items.bron: Seed germination produces a new plant (NCBI PMC8869448 'The Seed and the Metabolism Regulation'). 'Baie plante' correctly leaves room for spore plants such as ferns.

items.bewering: Die meeste lewende dinge gebruik suurstof om energie uit hulle kos te kry.
items.bron: BioNinja 'Mode of respiration' (ib.bioninja.com.au): most animals, plants and fungi are obligate aerobes; exceptions are obligate anaerobes (some bacteria, most archaea) and facultative anaerobes such as yeast. 'Die meeste' is the correctly softened quantifier; 'alle' would be false. Respiration releases energy from food (savemyexams.com).

items.bewering: Jy haal asem met jou longe, en 'n vis gebruik sy kieue.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Fish gill' and Macmillan Morris Biology ch. 39: gills on each side of the head extract oxygen from water; human gas exchange in the lungs (humanbiology.pressbooks.tru.ca 'Organs of Excretion' on CO2 leaving via the lungs).

items.bewering: 'n Plant neem ook lug in deur klein gaatjies in sy blare.
items.bron: EBSCO Research Starter 'Gas exchange in plants'; Oak National Academy 'Gas exchange and stomata': gases (carbon dioxide and oxygen) enter and leave the leaf by diffusion through stomata.

items.bewering: Elke lewende ding se liggaam maak afval wat moet uitkom.
items.bron: Excretion, removal of metabolic waste, is a characteristic of all living organisms (savemyexams.com IGCSE; vedantu.com 'Excretion and its importance').

items.bewering: Jy sweet, jy blaas lug uit en jy gaan toilet toe.
items.bron: Trinidad and Tobago Ministry of Education 'Excretion by the Lungs, Skin and Kidneys' (learn.moe.gov.tt) and humanbiology.pressbooks.tru.ca 16.2: skin removes water, salts and some urea in sweat; lungs remove carbon dioxide in exhaled air; kidneys remove urea in urine. Note: strictly, passing faeces is egestion rather than excretion, but 'toilet toe gaan' covers urinating and the simplification is standard and harmless at Grade 4.

items.bewering: 'n Plant maak kos en laat die suurstof wat oorbly deur sy blare uit.
items.bron: EBSCO 'Gas exchange in plants'; Oak National Academy stomata lesson: oxygen produced in photosynthesis leaves through the stomata. 'Wat oorbly' is accurate, since the plant uses some of that oxygen in its own respiration.

items.bewering: Elke lewende ding merk op wat om hom gebeur en reageer daarop.
items.bron: Sensitivity, detecting and responding to changes in the surroundings, is a characteristic of all living organisms (savemyexams.com IGCSE; vedantu.com 'Life processes').

items.bewering: Jy ruik die kos, en jy word honger.
items.bron: Zoon et al. 2016, Foods (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov PMC5224573): exposure to food odours increases appetite; cephalic-phase response to the smell of food. Everyday example, sound.

items.bewering: 'n Plant het nie oë of ore nie en merk tog die lig op.
items.bron: Macmillan 'The environmental context of growth and development' (digfir-published.macmillanusa.com hlw ch31): plants sense light direction with blue-light photoreceptors (phototropins) in the shoot tip. The comparison with eyes holds: it tells the learner sensing does not need eyes, which is true.

items.bewering: Lewende dinge beweeg self, party vinnig en party baie stadig.
items.bron: Movement of the whole organism or a part of it is a characteristic of living things; plants move by growing toward light (vedantu.com 'Life processes'; biologynotesonline.com). Read with the 'beweging' glossary entry, rooted plants are covered.

items.bewering: 'n Bok hardloop vir gevaar weg.
items.bron: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance 'Run and Hide' and Guinness World Records 'Fastest antelope' (springbok sprints and leaps to escape predators).

items.bewering: 'n Plant se stingel buig na die lig, en baie blomme maak saans toe.
items.bron: Phototropism: Macmillan hlw ch31 (shoot grows faster on the shaded side and bends toward light). Flowers closing at night (nyctinasty): Live Science 'Why do flowers close up at night?' (tulips, crocuses, poppies) and garden column listing African daisy (Gazania), a South African genus. 'Baie' correctly allows for night-opening flowers.

items.bewering: Party dinge lyk glad nie lewendig nie en leef tog. 'n Droë boontjie lê stil in 'n sakkie, maar in nat grond groei dit.
items.blok: Dinge wat nie lewendig lyk nie
items.bron: NCBI PMC8869448 'The Seed and the Metabolism Regulation': a dry seed is metabolically inactive but carries a living embryo; germination starts with water uptake. NDSU PLSC 368 ch. 7 on imbibition. True of a viable bean.

items.bewering: Droë gis word wakker in warm water met 'n bietjie suiker.
items.blok: Dinge wat nie lewendig lyk nie
items.bron: Williams-Sonoma 'Proofing yeast', Chowhound 'What does it mean to proof yeast?': active dry yeast is dormant and is activated in warm water with sugar. The mapping of 'wakker word' holds: a sleeper is alive but inactive, which is exactly the yeast's state.

items.bewering: Die gis kry kos uit die suiker en maak 'n gas as afval. Die gas vorm borrels in die water.
items.blok: Dinge wat nie lewendig lyk nie
items.bron: University at Buffalo news release 2020 'Meet baker's yeast': yeast digests sugar and releases carbon dioxide; proofing guides describe the resulting foam/bubbles as the sign the yeast is feeding.

items.bewering: Kos kry en afval uitkry is twee van die sewe lewensprosesse. Die borrels wys dat die gis doen wat lewende dinge doen.
items.blok: Dinge wat nie lewendig lyk nie
items.bron: Nutrition and excretion are two of the seven (twinkl.com; savemyexams.com). Carbon dioxide from a cell's energy release counts as excreted waste in the same way the lesson treats exhaled air. The claim is framed as evidence, not proof, which is sound.

items.bewering: In 'n bevrugte eier wag die begin van 'n klein kuiken. As die eier warm gehou word, groei die kuiken waar jy dit nie kan sien nie.
items.blok: Dinge wat nie lewendig lyk nie
items.bron: Penn State Extension 'Where chick life begins' (abe.psu.edu): when the laid egg cools, cell division of the blastoderm stops without killing the embryo, and it resumes when warmed by the hen or an incubator; poultry diapause literature (biorxiv 2022.02.23.481599) agrees. 'Wag' maps correctly onto this paused state.

items.bewering: Kieme is lewende dinge wat te klein is om te sien.
items.blok: Kieme is te klein om te sien
items.bron: KidsHealth 'What Are Germs?' (living things; need a microscope to see them); bio.libretexts.org NCSU MB352 'Introduction to the Microscope': unaided eye resolves about 0.1 mm, bacteria are about 1 micrometre. Same caveat on viruses as recorded under 'Baie soorte lewende dinge'.

items.bewering: Honderde kieme kan langs mekaar op die punt agter hierdie sin lê.
items.blok: Kieme is te klein om te sien
items.bron: microbeonline.com 'Size of bacteria': about 500 bacteria of 1 micrometre could lie end to end across a printed full stop; a university answer key gives about 1 000 in a period. A printed full stop is roughly 0.3-0.5 mm, so 'honderde langs mekaar' holds for typical bacteria; the comparison maps correctly (it is a row, and the dot could hold far more by area, which the sentence does not contradict).

items.bewering: Baie kieme eet, hulle groei en hulle maak nuwe kieme, net soos ander lewende dinge.
items.blok: Kieme is te klein om te sien
items.bron: KidsHealth 'What Are Germs?': bacteria take nutrients from their surroundings and multiply; viruses need living cells to reproduce. 'Baie' is the right quantifier, because viruses do not eat or grow on their own; 'alle kieme' would have been false.

items.bewering: Met 'n mikroskoop kan 'n mens hulle wel sien.
items.blok: Kieme is te klein om te sien
items.bron: bio.libretexts.org NCSU MB352: bacteria (about 1 micrometre) are visible with a light microscope; viruses need an electron microscope, which is still a microscope. KidsHealth agrees.

items.bewering: lewensprosesse: Die sewe dinge wat saam wys dat iets lewe.
items.bron: Seven-process convention (twinkl.com; savemyexams.com). Read alone it is accurate; it states the seven together are evidence of life, not that each must be visible at every moment, so it does not clash with the dry bean or egg.

items.bewering: voeding: Om kos te kry of kos te maak vir jou liggaam.
items.bron: Nutrition: obtaining food (animals) or making it (plants by photosynthesis) - vedantu.com 'Life processes'; savemyexams.com.

items.bewering: groei: Om groter en sterker te word en van binne te verander.
items.bron: Growth as permanent increase in size with development (vedantu.com 'Life processes'). 'Sterker' and 'van binne verander' are child-level glosses; read alone the entry leads to no false conclusion.

items.bewering: reproduseer: Om nuwe lewende dinge van jou eie soort te maak. Dit word ook voortplanting genoem.
items.bron: Reproduction defined as producing offspring of the same kind (savemyexams.com IGCSE); Afrikaans 'voortplanting' = reproduction (weet.co.za school material uses it in this sense).

items.bewering: asemhaling: Om energie uit jou kos te kry. Die meeste lewende dinge gebruik suurstof uit die lug of die water daarvoor.
items.bron: Respiration releases energy from food (savemyexams.com); most animals, plants and fungi are obligate aerobes (BioNinja 'Mode of respiration'), with aquatic organisms using oxygen dissolved in water (Wikipedia 'Fish gill'). 'Die meeste' is correct; 'alle' would be false.

items.bewering: uitskeiding: Om die afval wat jou liggaam maak weer uit te kry.
items.bron: Excretion: removal of metabolic waste made by the body (savemyexams.com IGCSE; learn.moe.gov.tt 'Excretion by the Lungs, Skin and Kidneys'). 'Afval wat jou liggaam maak' is the accurate wording.

items.bewering: sintuie: Die dele waarmee 'n lewende ding raaksien wat om hom gebeur.
items.bron: Sensitivity: detecting changes in the surroundings (savemyexams.com). 'Dele' is general enough to cover a plant's light-sensing shoot tip (Macmillan hlw ch31; Darwin's tip experiment), so it is consistent with the study text saying a plant has no eyes or ears.

items.bewering: beweging: Wanneer 'n hele lewende ding of net 'n deel daarvan beweeg.
items.bron: Movement: 'an action by an organism or part of an organism causing a change of position or place' (Cambridge IGCSE wording, via biologynotesonline.com and savemyexams.com).

items.bewering: kieue: Die dele langs 'n vis se kop waarmee hy in water asemhaal.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Fish gill': gills are housed on each side of the head beneath the operculum and take oxygen from water.

items.bewering: gis: 'n Klein lewende ding wat deeg laat rys.
items.bron: University at Buffalo 2020 release; Science News Explores 'Scientists Say: Yeast': a microscopic single-celled fungus whose carbon dioxide makes dough rise.

items.bewering: broodmuf: Muf wat op ou brood groei en van die brood leef.
items.bron: EBSCO Research Starter 'Black bread mold'; bio.libretexts.org 'Rhizopus'.

items.bewering: kieme: Baie klein lewende dinge wat 'n mens siek kan maak.
items.bron: KidsHealth 'What Are Germs?' ('tiny organisms, or living things, that can cause disease'); weet.co.za 'Oordraagbare siektes' (patogene soos bakterieë, virusse, swamme en parasiete). 'Kan' is correct, since many microbes are harmless. Read alone it holds; the debate about whether viruses are alive is noted under 'Selfs broodmuf en kieme is lewende dinge'.

items.bewering: mikroskoop: 'n Toestel wat baie klein goed baie groter laat lyk.
items.bron: bio.libretexts.org NCSU MB352 'Introduction to the Microscope': an instrument that magnifies objects too small for the eye.

items.bewering: bevrugte eier: 'n Eier waarin die begin van 'n kleintjie kan groei.
items.bron: Penn State Extension 'Where chick life begins': the fertilised egg carries the blastoderm that develops into the chick. 'Kan' correctly makes growth conditional (on warmth).

items.bewering: waterdamp: Water in die vorm van 'n gas wat niemand kan sien nie.
items.bron: London South Bank University water site (water.lsbu.ac.uk 'Steam'): water vapour is a transparent, invisible gas; the visible cloud is condensed droplets (curriculumvisions.com; Science Buddies).

items.bewering: 'n Plant op die vensterbank buig na die venster toe. Watter twee lewensprosesse kan jy hier raaksien?
items.bron: Phototropism shows sensing of light and movement of a part (Macmillan hlw ch31), so at least two processes are visible, as the question presupposes. For whoever writes a memo: the bending is produced by uneven growth, so a learner who answers 'groei' is also right and should not be marked wrong.

items.bewering: Noem drie dinge wat lyk of hulle nie leef nie, maar wat wel leef.
items.bron: The lesson's three examples (dry bean, dry yeast, fertilised egg) are each confirmed above (NCBI PMC8869448; yeast proofing sources; Penn State Extension).

opsomming: Every claim checks out against sources, the two 'die meeste' quantifiers are correctly softened and the analogies (waking yeast, the waiting egg, germs on a full stop) map soundly; the only point a person may want to know is that germs include viruses, whose living status scientists still debate, which the lesson handles acceptably for Grade 4 by never claiming what every germ does.
